headline: Discussed 195 Appleton Street purchase and a possible appraisal for Newton Street parcels; no votes were taken.
summary: The executive director said Bridgewater Capital Partners recently bought 195 Appleton Street, a property in the Urban Renewal Plan, and that the initial plan is housing. The South High Street study is nearly complete. Before paying O'Connell Development's final invoice, the authority asked to review the final report.
transcript:
# Holyoke Redevelopment Authority

## Meeting Minutes

Wednesday, August 19, 2026 at 5:00 pm

via Zoom Meeting ID: 81780964201

**Members Present:** Patrick Beaudry, Chairperson; Daphne Board, Treasurer; Karen Betournay, Member

**Staff Present:** Eric Nakajima, Executive Director; John Dyjach, Assistant Director

**Other(s) Present:** Vadim Tulchinsky, Urbanist Development

## 1. Call to Order

Patrick Beaudry called the meeting to order at 5:03 p.m. He announced that the meeting is being recorded and being held virtually in accordance with State law. A roll call followed:

| Member | Present |
|---|---|
| Patrick Beaudry | X |
| Karen Betournay | X |
| Daphne Board | X |

## 2. HRA Board Business

### a. Executive Director Report

Eric Nakajima informed the Board of the following:

- 195 Appleton Street was recently purchased by Bridgewater Capital Partners. He said this property is in the Urban Renewal Plan and especially important to downtown redevelopment. A meeting with developer is being scheduled and the initial information is that the development is for housing.

## 3. Property/Project Updates and Next Steps

### a. South High Street Reuse Analysis & Predevelopment Feasibility Study

John Dyjach said that the report is essentially complete with a final review pending with MassDevelopment. He asked the Board to consider the final invoice for the work that is due to O'Connell Development. After some discussion the Board requested that the final report be circulated to them for review before considering the payment. Eric Nakajima said that one of the ideas he has discussed with MassDevelopment is to development a web landing page explaining the purpose of the work along this section of High Street and how it relates to the Urban Renewal Plan.

### b. URP Area 4 - Newton Street Parcels- (possible vote on appraisal authorization)

John Dyjach said that the transfer of the Newton Street parcels from the City to the HRA is in process and that staff will present information on the request next Monday at the City Council Development and Government Relations Committee. He said that if the request is approved, staff would proceed with soliciting an appraisal which he believed the Board previously approved paying for the cost. Eric Nakajima said that in some instances the HRA will request that an appraisal requirement be waived by the State but the scope of this project justifies getting one done.

## 4. Other / New Business

### a. 

John Dyjach said that he expects the six-month update on the 123 Pine Street project to be made at the next HRA meeting. Patrick Beaudry said that it is especially helpful for him to get a first-hand look at the progress of developments and would welcome a visit to the property in the future if the owner is agreeable.

### b. 

Eric Nakajima noted the message from Vadim Tulchinsky inviting the HRA to a ribbon cutting for the new residences at the Crafts Block located at 147 High Street scheduled for 1 p.m. on September 1st.

## 5. Adjournment

A motion was made by Daphne Board to adjourn the meeting. Said motion was seconded by Karen Betournay and a roll call vote followed:

| Member | Yes | No |
|---|---|---|
| Daphne Board | X | |
| Karen Betournay | X | |
| Patrick Beaudry | X | |

The meeting was adjourned at 5:31 p.m.

Respectfully Submitted,

Patrick Beaudry, Chairperson
